newsitem.title: CANADA: TVX Gold confirms may suspend Greek work.
newsitem.headline: TVX Gold confirms may suspend Greek work.

text.p: TVX Gold Inc's vice-chairman confirmed on Tuesday that the company will suspend its multi-million-dollar project in northern Greece if local residents continue to disrupt work.
But John Hick said in a phone interview that he was confident the Greek government would intervene and remove the protesters before a suspension of operations was necessary.

"All we're saying is if that doesn't happen in a fairly short time frame, then until it does we're going to have to temporarily suspend operations," Hick said. Protests have hindered work at the project for 10 months.

TVX executive vice-president Costas Sinis was quoted in the Greek media on Tuesday as saying the company would temporarily shut down its Greek mines before the end of October unless the demonstrations were stopped.
Local residents have blocked the road leading to the mines, saying the company's gold processing plant threatened the area's tourism business and the environment.
Although TVX had continued some work on the project, the protesters prevented the company from bringing in heavy machinery, said Hick.
"We don't have full access to what we want to do."
TVX has repeatedly asked the government to remove roadblocks, but Hick said Tuesday he was confident the government would take quick action.

"I'm very confident that they are serious about how important this project is for Greece," he said. "They can't afford to have this project -- which is the largest private investment in years -- fail."
He said government officials had told him they would secure full access to the mines.
"We own the mines there and we have no intention of walking away from that investment," he said.
TVX closed its US$270 million purchase of the Kassandra mines last December. It has invested $28 million in development so far, Hick said.
The company is relying on the mines to keep its promise to shareholders to produce 1.1 million ounces of gold a year by the year 2000, versus 423,000 ounces in 1995.
The property so far is expected to produce 300,000 ounces of gold a year at a cash cost of US$150 an ounce, company officials have said.
TVX employs about 650 people at the project and is the largest employer in the area, Hick said.
